answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may place orders, then slash that stake when independent counterparties prove repeated fraud under a fixed dispute rule. A newcomer can still participate, but flooding the market with aliases ties up capital in every account, while detected abuse destroys some of it. The stake is not proof of personhood: it makes Sybil attacks costly, especially when an island market, a ridge of scarce liquidity, or a wharf’s limited trading slots rewards only a few active identities.
